blocks.text: The solubility of an ionic compound in water depends on the balance of two energy changes.

items: Enthalpy of hydration: the energy released when gaseous ions are surrounded and attracted by water molecules; always exothermic. Smaller ions with higher charge density attract water more strongly, giving a more negative value; it becomes less negative down a group as ions grow.

Lattice enthalpy: the energy needed to break one mole of an ionic solid into gaseous ions; always endothermic. It is larger when the attractive forces are stronger, which depends on the charges and sizes of the ions: when cation and anion are of comparable size the lattice energy is high, and when one ion is much larger than the other it is lower.

blocks.text: The enthalpy of solution is the overall energy change when a solid ionic substance dissolves; a more negative (or less positive) value generally favours higher solubility.

blocks.alt: Two bar charts on a log scale from the book's Table 17.4. Hydroxides: Mg(OH)2 2 x 10^-5, Ca(OH)2 1.5 x 10^-3, Sr(OH)2 3.4 x 10^-3 and Ba(OH)2 1.5 x 10^-2 mol per 100 g water, rising down the group. Sulphates: MgSO4 0.183, CaSO4 4.66 x 10^-3, SrSO4 7.11 x 10^-5 and BaSO4 9.43 x 10^-7, falling down the group.
blocks.caption: Solubility trends of Group 2 hydroxides and sulphates (original chart after Figure 17.4 and Table 17.4).
blocks.long_description: The solubilities of Group 2 compounds show opposite trends. Hydroxides become more soluble down the group: magnesium hydroxide is sparingly soluble, barium hydroxide quite soluble. Sulphates become less soluble down the group: magnesium sulphate is soluble while barium sulphate is almost insoluble. Each trend comes from how the lattice enthalpy and the hydration enthalpy change as the cation grows, and the bars are drawn on a log scale because the values span six powers of ten.

items: Hydroxides: solubility increases down the group (Mg(OH)2 sparingly soluble, Ba(OH)2 quite soluble). Both hydration and lattice enthalpies decrease down the group, but for the small hydroxide ion the fall in lattice enthalpy is the larger, so dissolving becomes easier.

Sulphates: solubility decreases down the group (MgSO4 soluble, BaSO4 insoluble). The sulphate ion is large, so the lattice enthalpy changes little as the cation grows, while the hydration enthalpy falls more; dissolving becomes harder.

blocks.caption: Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides and sulphates at 298 K, mol per 100 g water (book's Table 17.4)

blocks.prompt: Which is more soluble, Sr(OH)2 or Mg(OH)2? Give the reason.
blocks.explanation: Sr(OH)2 (3.4 x 10^-3 against 2 x 10^-5 mol/100 g): down the group the lattice enthalpy of the hydroxides falls more than the hydration enthalpy, so they dissolve more easily.

items: Solubility depends on lattice enthalpy versus hydration enthalpy.
Hydroxides: more soluble down the group; sulphates: less soluble down the group.
